A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FrontierCO. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original solver evaluations across eight CO problems in Tables 3–6, plus neural-module ablations and STP training experiments in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains those original benchmark evaluations and reports additional SIL, fast-configuration TSP, and asymmetric TSP results.

M1.justification: No new proposed algorithmic component is introduced. The existing STP prediction-and-decoding procedure remains unchanged; SIL and RRNCO are additional evaluated baselines, while Appendix C documents implementation details.

E1.justification: The original eight problem collections remain, but Appendix F adds a distinct non-Euclidean, non-metric asymmetric TSP benchmark from real-world applications: 31 easy and 33 hard instances. This substantively extends routing coverage beyond v1's symmetric two-dimensional Euclidean TSP.

E2.justification: V2 adds SIL to the existing TSP and CVRP comparisons and evaluates RRNCO on the added ATSP benchmark. Section 5.1 removes the CVRP ablation comparing DeepACO, ACO, and HGS; DeepACO and HGS remain in the main CVRP comparison. Most comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: The principal one-hour budget, hardware, primal-gap metric, and aggregation rules remain. Appendix E adds fast TSP configurations: LKH-3 with POPMUSIC and 1,000 trials, greedy LEHD, DIFUSCO with 50 steps and greedy decoding, and SIL with 10 reconstruction steps. These are additional protocols; Appendix C's newly disclosed settings do not establish revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantive analyses of efficiency across TSP instance sizes and difficulty on non-Euclidean ATSP instances in Appendices E–F. It removes the DeepACO–ACO neural-module ablation, including the case where the neural component did not improve quality. The STP learning-curve analysis and LLM algorithm word cloud are retained.

E5.justification: V1's detailed tables report point estimates. V2 adds ± dispersion values for primal gaps and geometric standard deviations for solving times throughout Tables 4–11. This substantially expands statistical reporting, although repeated-run counts, seeds, and the sampling basis of the gap dispersion remain unspecified; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: V2 adds SIL results, aggregate LLM scores, fast TSP results, and ATSP results. SIL's TSP gaps are 2.51%/21.34% on easy/hard sets; the new ATSP hard-set gaps are 15.46% for RRNCO and 0.08% for LKH-3. Among matched entries, DiffUCO's easy-MIS gap changes from 9.57% to 9.54%, and IL-LNS/CL-LNS easy-CPMP times change from 3600s to 2636s/2649s. CVRP ablation entries are removed; most other retained means are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1's formal algorithm-search objective and associated search-space definitions in Equation 3. It explicitly formulates per-instance minimization and explains negating maximization objectives, including MIS. The primal-gap formula remains unchanged, and neither version contains substantial theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central benchmark contribution and overall classical-solver advantage remain. V2 narrows the conclusion from LLM 'novel strategy discovery' to better use of existing algorithms, and from neural excellence on structured problems to improving certain human heuristics. The introduction also drops the absolute claim that the hard set is immune to heuristic hacking.

C2.justification: V2 shifts the explanation of LLM variability from solver selection/integration toward a hypothesis about inability to assess generated algorithms, adding applicability concerns for hard-to-verify tasks. It expands memory and inference-bottleneck explanations and adds deployment-cost tradeoffs in Appendix G. V1's explicit reference-solution construction-cost limitation and interpretation of the unsuccessful DeepACO ablation are removed.

D1.justification: V1 provides hardware, data generators, and an example prompt but omits many solver-specific settings. V2's Appendix C supplies checkpoint sources, training sample counts, inference settings, and agent search parameters, including Self-Refine's o4-mini configuration, 64 iterations, and development timeout. It also adds a project code-repository link and discloses discarded route-length constraints in eight Golden instances.

R1.justification: Section 6 extends benchmark positioning through RL4CO, Jumanji, ML4CO-bench-101, Routing Arena, and ML4TSPBench, and adds work such as AlphaEvolve and SPL-LNS. Further citations support the metric and new analyses. These are limited extensions of the retained neural/symbolic framing and realism/scalability motivation.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the title, abstract, introduction, results narrative, and conclusion. It reorganizes the appendices around implementation details, moves the existing prompt into Appendix C.3, adds a reproducibility statement, and removes the acknowledgements and standalone impact/limitations paragraphs. The changes extend well beyond isolated wording edits.

P2.justification: V2 simplifies Figure 1, redraws Figure 2 with SIL and failure markers while removing numerical labels, and removes the classical-runtime chart. It splits the paired result tables into individual problem tables with dispersion reporting, reduces the ablation table, and adds aggregate, efficiency, and ATSP tables. Typography and page layout are extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's missing reproducibility information through checkpoint provenance and detailed solver/agent settings. Dispersion reporting and the new efficiency and non-Euclidean evaluations strengthen evidence for the benchmark's central concerns. Removing the unfavorable DeepACO ablation reduces balance, and stronger explanations of LLM failures remain insufficiently tested, but the gains in reproducibility and empirical support outweigh these drawbacks.
